item.title: Tim Curry trivia
item.description:
In memory of the prolific actor and icon Tim Curry (1946 - 2026), and among countless topics, this is a look at his professional rivalry and friendship with Ian McKellen.
Curry portrayed Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and McKellen his competitor Antonio Salieri when the new play Amadeus (1979) premiered on Broadway in 1980. During their time together on stage was Constanze Weber, the beloved of Mozart, at first portrayed by Jane Seymour (above) and later by Amy Irving.
In 1968 Curry was in the stage play Hair in London, and partied with McKellen due to shared social circles. Curry became known for The Rocky Horror Show in 1973, and on becoming co-stars in 1980 McKellen recalls on mckellen.com: “I had known Tim long before he struck stardom with the original stage production of Rocky Horror Picture Show. All in all I was looking forward to being back with old friends on Broadway...”
Curry in his memoir Vagabond (2025) wrote about their Broadway collaboration: “I liked him enough when we were acquaintances, though once we started Amadeus, our relationship became intensely competitive.”
“There were some strange points of jealousy and strain, and I suppose it’s accurate to say we had quite a rivalry while doing the play, and even a few confrontations—nothing physical, of course. We are both very British, so any discord between us was harmless. As a matter of fact, it ultimately provided valuable energy for the play.” (photo by Zoë Dominic).
“There was a legitimate rivalry between Mozart and Salieri. The tension between me and Ian made sense in the wider scheme of the plot and never distorted the performance. And that’s all that mattered to either of us.”
The role earned Curry his first Tony Award nomination in 1981, for ’Best Performance by a Leading Actor in a Play’, but he lost to McKellen. Though Curry in 2015 would call it his favourite stage production, both he and McKellen left for new work in 1981. Note: later Curry won ’Best Actor in a Musical’ for My Favorite Year (1992) and for Spamalot (2005).
The two actors were reunited, on the silver screen, in the comic book film The Shadow (1994). The official FB page Tim Curry News reports that Curry later shared: “It was terrific that he was doing The Shadow because we’d been friends for 20 years. We had a lot of fun on the set because we don’t take each other very seriously.”
They could even been reunited a second time; Crawley's Casting Calls reports on The Lord of the Rings (2001 - 2003) that if the primary choice for the wizard Saruman, Christopher Lee (1922 - 2015), had declined then director Peter Jackson considered actors as Tim Curry, Jeremy Irons, and Malcolm McDowell for the role (image by Geek Dave).

item.title: This is Paris
item.description: Let's go to 1997 Paris Hilton is 16 year old . She's a normal rebellious teen that sneaks out and skips school Her parents, don't know what to do with her ,so they hire strangers to take her away At 2 am ,two men walk into her bedroom and drag her out of the house while she screams Her parents watch it happens. They've been told it's for her own good She ends up at Provo canyon school in Utah,a boarding school for troubled teens She's strip searched the day she arrives. She's hit and choked by the staff. She's forced to take pills that nobody explain to her what are for When she acts out they lock her in a bare room for 24 hours She stays there for 11 months Provo is part of something called the troubled teen industry, a billion dollars business Parents pay huge amounts of money to send difficult kids away , and for over 50 years, nobody watched what happens inside Kids came out telling horror stories. Adults call them liars and the money kept rolling in Then that industry made their biggest mistake,they hurt Paris In September 2020, Paris releases on YouTube called "This is Paris" Everyone expects a fun movie about a rich glamorous life Instead,she sits down and tells the world,on camera,for the first time ever, what happened to her at the Provo canyon. Even her own family didn't know the details until they saw the film Over 50 million people watch , and she says the school name,out loud on the record ,for everyone to hear But she doesn't stop at a documentary One month later,she gets on a plane to Utah and leads a silent protest right outside the gates of Provo canyon school Hundreds of survivors march beside her. Some of them were locked up there at the same time she was Imagine standing in front of the place that tortured you and refusing to look away . That's what she did Then she takes the fight to the government In February 2021, she testifies in front of the Utah state Senate. She tells a room full of politicians, in detail, what that school did to her Utah passes a law to finally regulate those facilities. It passes almost unanimously Then she does it again,in Minnesota, in Oregon and in California In total,she helps pass 15 paws across the country. Fifteen. She spends years meeting with members of Congress , pushing for one thing, a federal law that protects kids in those facilities in every state The woman they mocked as "the dumb blonde" for 20 years just outworked the United States Congress December 2024, it finally happens The Stop Institutional Child Abuse Act becomes federal law . It passed the Senate unanimously For the first time in American history, there's a national law law taking on the abuse inside those facilities Paris words that day : " I did this for the younger version of myself" The little girl nobody saved grew up and saved everyone else And now,in July 2026 , the final blow The state of Utah revokes Provo canyon school license after finding 16 serious allegations Investigators found a girl whose kidneys have failed,after staff ignored her pain for over a week A 13 year old boy was left with a brain injury and a broken jaw ,and nobody called 911 Every child inside was moved out by August 6 . The owners are banned for reopening for 5 years The school that tortured her is closing , because of her

item.title: GovBrief Today #573
item.description: Twenty-four states took the Supreme Court up on its dare in two days. On Monday the Court unblocked Donald Trump's mail voting order, ruling the states sued too soon because courts only review final rules. The final rule says the USPS will not deliver your ballot unless the envelope carries a tracking barcode and your name and address match a federal list the agency admits is partly for law enforcement. The Postal Service issued that rule on Friday, three days before the justices called the case premature. Wednesday morning, 10 weeks before Election Day, the states returned to court with the receipts. I've emailed 8,822 stories over 573 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I will. item.title: Trans Dating - Lost and Found
item.description: I have been posting these cause you all seem to love them (some of you too much, my DMs here on imgur have blow up since starting this series...) Anyway, context before the comments inevitably do what they have on these posts: These videos start where the actual conversation started. The messages you see at the beginning are the first DMs these guys sent me... I’m not cutting out some earlier conversation that makes them make more sense. My dating profile also explicitly says that I’m trans and pre-op. They know. I promise, you do not need to accuse me of being the stereotype... I generally only turn conversations into videos when they eventually get weird, hostile, or the guy turns on me. Often I leave that part out because the interaction is funnier without it, or because I’d rather end on the joke than the ugliness. Obligatory wholesome disclaimer: All of the ad revenue from my YouTube channel goes to trans charities. So if you watch these idiots be idiots over there, they accidentally help trans people. Which remains one of my favorite parts of this entire project. I’ve also genuinely loved posting these because it’s given me another way to connect with other trans folks over the shared absurdity of trying to date while trans. item.title: WTF!
item.description: morbidtruth Former San Antonio wills and trusts attorney Karen Kay Hogan, 69, was sentenced on June 1, 2026, to 20 years in prison for stealing $541,550 from six orphaned siblings. The children, ranging from 4 to 15 years old, had lost both of their parents in a tragic manner in December 2021 in Boerne, Texas. Hogan had been appointed independent administrator of the parents’ estate but used her position to systematically take funds for her own personal expenses. The six children were the sole heirs to the estate of Jason and Emily Evans, and the oldest child has a developmental disability. Hogan opened unauthorized bank accounts in the deceased parents’ names, listed herself as a joint owner, and funneled insurance proceeds and estate funds out of the accounts without court permission. In March 2026, she accepted a plea deal and pleaded guilty to misapplication of fiduciary property over $300,000, a first-degree felony, and explo-tation of a child/disabled individual, a third-degree felony. Judge Kirsten Cohoon sentenced Hogan in Kendall County to the maximum 20-year prison term. She was also ordered to pay a $5,000 fine and $189,678.50 in outstanding restitution. Before sentencing, Hogan voluntarily surrendered her Texas law license.
